waste_flags.message: Flood irrigation on corn loses about 22 acre-ft per year compared with drip.
Flood irrigation on oats loses about 2.7 acre-ft per year compared with drip.

assumptions: Mature, full-producing orchards.
Weather is regional (NASA POWER grid cell about 50 km wide).
Yield losses from weather and water only. Nutrients, pests, and disease are assumed well managed.
Reference ET0 is FAO-56 Penman-Monteith from NASA POWER daily weather.
Crop water use is ETc = Kc x ET0 with the FAO-56 single crop coefficient curve.
Effective rain: rain under 5 mm in a day is lost, and 80 percent of larger rains reach the root zone (Dastane 1974, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 25).
Irrigation refills the root zone when half of the available water is used (FAO-56 soil water balance). The root zone starts each season full.
Relative yield uses FAO-33: 1 - Ya/Ym = Ky x (1 - ETa/ETc). Each heat stress day above this location's normal count takes another 0.25 percent off, up to 10 percent.
Seasons that cross the new year are counted in the year they end.
Dormant orchards and alfalfa are not irrigated outside their growing season.
Some crop parameters are placeholders still being checked against FAO sources: almonds, corn, oats, processing_tomatoes.
Almond yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Walnut yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Alfalfa hay yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Almond production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Walnut production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Processing tomato production cost uses the San Joaquin Valley South study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
No production cost study for oat in any region, so it has no production cost.
Surface water price uses a typical Merced Irrigation District value. Actual district rates vary.
Cost estimate: The Sacramento Valley study prices no drip system; the San Joaquin Valley South 2024 study's system cost is used.
Cost estimate: National/regional ERS average; no California oats cost study available.
Cost estimate: National ERS average; no California oats cost study..
Revenue uses the same median-normalized harvest quantity as the harvest-weight display.
Prices: each year uses that year's USDA NASS price.
Costs: each year's UC Davis study costs are scaled to that year by USDA NASS prices-paid indexes and U.S. EIA diesel and electricity prices.
Applied water is 35% surface water at $50 per acre-ft and 65% groundwater pumped from 150 ft (about $39 per acre-ft at 2016 electricity prices).
The summary's high, low, and typical years are ranked by farm profit.
Harvest weight is the selected county or statewide median yield scaled by how each year's relative yield compares with this block's median year, so a typical year shows a typical county harvest.
Frost occurred within 45 days of planting in 5 of 5 years for block b4 (oats planted in Nov).

summary.avg_cost.label: Estimated cost per year
summary.avg_cost.formula_text: Sum of yearly farm cost / number of years with price data, 2012 to 2016

inputs.name: Farm cost, 2012
inputs.source: Calculated each year as inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system. Inputs, harvest and irrigation system come from the cost studies (Almonds: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Almonds, Sacramento Valley, 2024, p. 19 (used because San Joaquin Valley North has no almonds study); Processing tomatoes: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Processing tomatoes, San Joaquin Valley South, 2018, p. 14 (used because San Joaquin Valley North has no processing tomatoes study); Corn: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Corn, San Joaquin Valley North, 2015, p. 11; Oats: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns, oats, U.S. total (no California study)), scaled to that year's input prices (nearest year when missing) by the USDA NASS Prices Paid Index (2011=100) and the U.S. EIA diesel price, times acres (harvest times simulated tons). Water is the acre-ft applied (YieldGenerator simulation using NASA POWER weather, NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2012 to 2016) priced at Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/acre-ft); 2022 drought rate was $100/acre-ft for surface water and at the U.S. EIA California commercial electricity price for well pumping.

block.b1.2012.profit.label: Estimated margin, Almonds, 2012
block.b1.2012.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2012.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 1,960 lb/acre / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 40 acres = 39.20 tons
Sales: 39.20 tons x 2,000 lb/ton x $2.58 per lb = $202,272
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 101.4 / 101.2 = 1.001976
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 105.4 / 117 = 0.900855
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 102.9 / 171 = 0.601754
EIA diesel price ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: $3.968 / $3.76 = 1.055319
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $2,074.33 per acre x 40 acres = $82,973.20
Harvest cost: 39.20 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 1.055319 diesel ratio = $25,761.297299, rounded to $25,761.30
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.907305 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,840.260235, rounded to $2,840.26
Surface water: 139.3775 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.782125 acre-ft, rounded to 48.7821 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.7821 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,439.105, rounded to $2,439.11
Groundwater: 139.3775 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.595375 acre-ft, rounded to 90.5954 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.5954 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1341 per kWh = $3,110.103844, rounded to $3,110.10
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,439.11 + groundwater pumping $3,110.10 = $5,549.21
Cost: inputs $82,973.20 + harvest $25,761.30 + water $5,549.21 + irrigation system $2,840.26 = $117,123.97, rounded to $117,124

block.b1.2012.cost.label: Estimated cost, Almonds, 2012
block.b1.2012.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2012.cost.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1.

steps.text: NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 101.4 / 101.2 = 1.001976
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 105.4 / 117 = 0.900855
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 102.9 / 171 = 0.601754
EIA diesel price ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: $3.968 / $3.76 = 1.055319
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $2,074.33 per acre x 40 acres = $82,973.20
Harvest cost: 39.2 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 1.055319 diesel ratio = $25,761.297299, rounded to $25,761.30
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.907305 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,840.260235, rounded to $2,840.26
Surface water: 139.3775 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.782125 acre-ft, rounded to 48.7821 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.7821 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,439.105, rounded to $2,439.11
Groundwater: 139.3775 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.595375 acre-ft, rounded to 90.5954 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.5954 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1341 per kWh = $3,110.103844, rounded to $3,110.10
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,439.11 + groundwater pumping $3,110.10 = $5,549.21
Cost: inputs $82,973.20 + harvest $25,761.30 + water $5,549.21 + irrigation system $2,840.26 = $117,123.97, rounded to $117,124

block.b1.2013.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system

steps.text: NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2013 / 2024 study year: 96.7 / 101.2 = 0.955534
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2013 / 2024 study year: 108.5 / 117 = 0.927350
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2013 / 2024 study year: 106.3 / 171 = 0.621637

Inputs cost: $2,076.89 per acre x 40 acres = $83,075.60
Harvest cost: 39.2 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 1.043085 diesel ratio = $25,462.654224, rounded to $25,462.65
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.905418 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,834.353102, rounded to $2,834.35
Surface water: 139.3691 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.779185 acre-ft, rounded to 48.7792 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.7792 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,438.96
Groundwater: 139.3691 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.589915 acre-ft, rounded to 90.5899 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.5899 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.142 per kWh = $3,293.124045, rounded to $3,293.12
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,438.96 + groundwater pumping $3,293.12 = $5,732.08

block.b1.2016.profit.label: Estimated margin, Almonds, 2016
block.b1.2016.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2016.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 1,960 lb/acre / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 40 acres = 39.20 tons
Sales: 39.20 tons x 2,000 lb/ton x $2.39 per lb = $187,376
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2016 / 2024 study year: 71.8 / 101.2 = 0.709486
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2016 / 2024 study year: 107.7 / 117 = 0.920513
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2016 / 2024 study year: 115.9 / 171 = 0.677778
EIA diesel price ratio, 2016 / 2024 study year: $2.304 / $3.76 = 0.612766
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $1,796.03 per acre x 40 acres = $71,841.20
Harvest cost: 39.20 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 0.612766 diesel ratio = $14,958.175775, rounded to $14,958.18
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.718707 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,249.866266, rounded to $2,249.87
Surface water: 138.9953 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.648355 acre-ft, rounded to 48.6484 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.6484 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,432.42
Groundwater: 138.9953 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.346945 acre-ft, rounded to 90.3469 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.3469 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1507 per kWh = $3,485.511124, rounded to $3,485.51
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,432.42 + groundwater pumping $3,485.51 = $5,917.93
Cost: inputs $71,841.20 + harvest $14,958.18 + water $5,917.93 + irrigation system $2,249.87 = $94,967.18, rounded to $94,967

steps.text: Harvest: 47.845 tons/acre x 1 / 1 x 80.5 acres = 3,851.5225 tons, rounded to 3,851.52 tons
Sales: 3,851.52 tons x $98.60 per ton = $379,759.872, rounded to $379,760

NASS chemicals index ratio, 2014 / 2018 study year: 109.5 / 102.3 = 1.070381

Inputs cost: $2,487.28 per acre x 80.5 acres = $200,226.04
Harvest cost: 3,851.52 tons x $6.50 per ton x 1.203587 diesel ratio = $30,131.656115, rounded to $30,131.66
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $750 / 25 + $300 / 3 = $130.0000
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $130.0000 per acre per year x 1.085250 weighted ratio x 80.5 acres = $11,357.14125, rounded to $11,357.14
Surface water: 300.9022 acre-ft x 0.35 = 105.31577 acre-ft, rounded to 105.3158 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 105.3158 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $5,265.79
Groundwater: 300.9022 acre-ft x 0.65 = 195.58643 acre-ft, rounded to 195.5864 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 195.5864 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1562 per kWh = $7,820.952494, rounded to $7,820.95
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $5,265.79 + groundwater pumping $7,820.95 = $13,086.74

block.b2.2015.profit.label: Estimated margin, Processing tomatoes, 2015
block.b2.2015.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b2.2015.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 47.845 tons/acre x 1 / 1 x 80.5 acres = 3,851.5225 tons, rounded to 3,851.52 tons
Sales: 3,851.52 tons x $93 per ton = $358,191.36, rounded to $358,191
NASS seeds index ratio, 2015 / 2018 study year: 124.6 / 115.6 = 1.077855
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2015 / 2018 study year: 87.2 / 70.1 = 1.243937
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2015 / 2018 study year: 106.5 / 102.3 = 1.041056
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2015 / 2018 study year: 111.9 / 126.3 = 0.885986
EIA diesel price ratio, 2015 / 2018 study year: $2.707 / $3.178 = 0.851794
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $6.50 per ton x 58 tons = $377
Inputs cost: $2,399.43 per acre x 80.5 acres = $193,154.115, rounded to $193,154.12
Harvest cost: 3,851.52 tons x $6.50 per ton x 0.851794 diesel ratio = $21,324.560575, rounded to $21,324.56
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $750 / 25 + $300 / 3 = $130.0000
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $130.0000 per acre per year x 1.003895 weighted ratio x 80.5 acres = $10,505.761175, rounded to $10,505.76
Surface water: 300.9022 acre-ft x 0.35 = 105.31577 acre-ft, rounded to 105.3158 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 105.3158 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $5,265.79
Groundwater: 300.9022 acre-ft x 0.65 = 195.58643 acre-ft, rounded to 195.5864 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 195.5864 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1573 per kWh = $7,876.029624, rounded to $7,876.03
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $5,265.79 + groundwater pumping $7,876.03 = $13,141.82
Cost: inputs $193,154.12 + harvest $21,324.56 + water $13,141.82 + irrigation system $10,505.76 = $238,126.26, rounded to $238,126

steps.text: Harvest: 47.845 tons/acre x 1 / 1 x 80.5 acres = 3,851.5225 tons, rounded to 3,851.52 tons
Sales: 3,851.52 tons x $86.30 per ton = $332,386.176, rounded to $332,386
NASS seeds index ratio, 2016 / 2018 study year: 121.4 / 115.6 = 1.050173
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2016 / 2018 study year: 71.8 / 70.1 = 1.024251
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2016 / 2018 study year: 107.7 / 102.3 = 1.052786
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2016 / 2018 study year: 115.9 / 126.3 = 0.917656
EIA diesel price ratio, 2016 / 2018 study year: $2.304 / $3.178 = 0.724984
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $6.50 per ton x 58 tons = $377
Inputs cost: $2,266.39 per acre x 80.5 acres = $182,444.395, rounded to $182,444.40
Harvest cost: 3,851.52 tons x $6.50 per ton x 0.724984 diesel ratio = $18,149.887442, rounded to $18,149.89
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $750 / 25 + $300 / 3 = $130.0000
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $130.0000 per acre per year x 0.937161 weighted ratio x 80.5 acres = $9,807.389865, rounded to $9,807.39
Surface water: 300.9823 acre-ft x 0.35 = 105.343805 acre-ft, rounded to 105.3438 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 105.3438 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $5,267.19
Groundwater: 300.9823 acre-ft x 0.65 = 195.638495 acre-ft, rounded to 195.6385 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 195.6385 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1507 per kWh = $7,547.576819, rounded to $7,547.58
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $5,267.19 + groundwater pumping $7,547.58 = $12,814.77
Cost: inputs $182,444.40 + harvest $18,149.89 + water $12,814.77 + irrigation system $9,807.39 = $223,216.45, rounded to $223,216

inputs.source: Calculated from crop water use vs the water the crop actually got (FAO-56 water balance on NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2016-04-01 to 2016-09-30) using the FAO-33 yield response factor Ky = 1.05 for processing tomatoes (FAO-66, Table 1, printed p. 7), minus a penalty for heat days above this crop's normal, counted from NASA POWER daily highs above 35 C (source not yet verified). The heat penalty (0.25% per extra day, at most 10%) is a team assumption, not a published value.

block.b3.2013.cost.label: Estimated cost, Corn, 2013
block.b3.2013.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system

steps.text: NASS seeds index ratio, 2013 / 2015 study year: 110.2 / 124.6 = 0.884430
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2013 / 2015 study year: 96.7 / 87.2 = 1.108945
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2013 / 2015 study year: 108.5 / 106.5 = 1.018779
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2013 / 2015 study year: 106.3 / 111.9 = 0.949955
EIA diesel price ratio, 2013 / 2015 study year: $3.922 / $2.707 = 1.448836

Weighted ratio for costs with no index of their own (other inputs, irrigation system): ($67 x 0.884430 + $230 x 1.108945 + $44 x 1.018779 + $173 x 0.949955 + $131 x 1.448836) / ($67 + $230 + $44 + $173 + $131) = 1.105861
Inputs cost: $796.22 per acre x 15 acres = $11,943.30
Harvest cost: 65.65 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system (flood) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $9 / 15 + $1 / 15 = $0.666667, rounded to $0.6667
Irrigation system cost (flood, installed cost / life): $0.6667 per acre per year x 1.105861 weighted ratio x 15 acres = $11.059163, rounded to $11.06
Surface water: 65.342 acre-ft x 0.35 = 22.8697 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 22.8697 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $1,143.485, rounded to $1,143.49
Groundwater: 65.342 acre-ft x 0.65 = 42.4723 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 42.4723 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.142 per kWh = $1,543.95305, rounded to $1,543.95
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $1,143.49 + groundwater pumping $1,543.95 = $2,687.44
Cost: inputs $11,943.30 + harvest $0.00 + water $2,687.44 + irrigation system $11.06 = $14,641.80, rounded to $14,642

block.b3.2014.cost.label: Estimated cost, Corn, 2014
block.b3.2014.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b3.2014.cost.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1.

steps.text: NASS seeds index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 113.5 / 124.6 = 0.910915
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 94.5 / 87.2 = 1.083716
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 109.5 / 106.5 = 1.028169
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 108 / 111.9 = 0.965147
EIA diesel price ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: $3.825 / $2.707 = 1.413003

Weighted ratio for costs with no index of their own (other inputs, irrigation system): ($67 x 0.910915 + $230 x 1.083716 + $44 x 1.028169 + $173 x 0.965147 + $131 x 1.413003) / ($67 + $230 + $44 + $173 + $131) = 1.097053
Inputs cost: $789.88 per acre x 15 acres = $11,848.20
Harvest cost: 65.65 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system (flood) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $9 / 15 + $1 / 15 = $0.666667, rounded to $0.6667
Irrigation system cost (flood, installed cost / life): $0.6667 per acre per year x 1.097053 weighted ratio x 15 acres = $10.971079, rounded to $10.97
Surface water: 65.342 acre-ft x 0.35 = 22.8697 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 22.8697 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $1,143.485, rounded to $1,143.49
Groundwater: 65.342 acre-ft x 0.65 = 42.4723 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 42.4723 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1562 per kWh = $1,698.348355, rounded to $1,698.35
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $1,143.49 + groundwater pumping $1,698.35 = $2,841.84
Cost: inputs $11,848.20 + harvest $0.00 + water $2,841.84 + irrigation system $10.97 = $14,701.01, rounded to $14,701

Irrigation system cost (flood, installed cost / life): $0.6667 per acre per year x 0.914477 weighted ratio x 15 acres = $9.145227, rounded to $9.15

block.b4.2016.cost.label: Estimated cost, Oats, 2016
block.b4.2016.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b4.2016.cost.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1.

steps.text: Inputs per acre (that year's USDA ERS values, not index scaled): $19.51 + $43.05 + $7.68 + $40.44 + $12.02 = $122.70
Inputs cost: $122.70 per acre x 12 acres = $1,472.40
Harvest cost: 16.63 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system cost (flood) (USDA ERS whole-farm average per planted acre already includes these costs; no separate irrigation system line): $0 per acre per year x 12 acres = $0.00
Surface water: 8.0986 acre-ft x 0.35 = 2.83451 acre-ft, rounded to 2.8345 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 2.8345 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $141.725, rounded to $141.73
Groundwater: 8.0986 acre-ft x 0.65 = 5.26409 acre-ft, rounded to 5.2641 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 5.2641 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1507 per kWh = $203.084767, rounded to $203.08
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $141.73 + groundwater pumping $203.08 = $344.81
Cost: inputs $1,472.40 + harvest $0.00 + water $344.81 + irrigation system $0.00 = $1,817.21, rounded to $1,817

Inputs, harvest and irrigation system come from the cost studies (Oats: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns, oats, U.S. total (no California study)), scaled to that year's input prices (nearest year when missing) by the USDA NASS Prices Paid Index (2011=100) and the U.S. EIA diesel price, times acres (harvest times simulated tons). Water is the acre-ft applied (YieldGenerator simulation using NASA POWER weather, NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2012 to 2016) priced at Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/acre-ft); 2022 drought rate was $100/acre-ft for surface water and at the U.S. EIA California commercial electricity price for well pumping.
